title: ThinkLeap: Reasoning Optimization Through Confidence-Guided Cognitive Leap Extraction

authors.text: Yijia Zhu, Zhenning Shi, Junhan Shi,

summary: Compressing long reasoning chains by preserving the cognitive leaps that matter.
abstract: ThinkLeap uses token-level confidence dynamics to locate critical transitions in a model's reasoning. It retains useful reasoning segments and replaces redundant deliberation with ellipsis markers, then uses these compact traces for self-distillation. Experiments on ARC-Challenge, GSM8K and MATH500 report an average 19.4% reduction in reasoning length while maintaining accuracy.

title: STIR: Self-Distilled Latent Tools for Dynamic Control of LLM Reasoning

authors.text: Zhenning Shi, Yijia Zhu, Junhan Shi,

summary: A self-distilled library of latent tools for selective, state-aware reasoning control.
abstract: STIR learns state-conditioned correction vectors from a model's own successful and failed reasoning trajectories. At structured checkpoints, it retrieves candidate tools and uses short lookahead rollouts to decide whether to intervene or abstain. Across six reasoning benchmarks, it improves average accuracy by 1.9% to 7.5% over vanilla decoding and reduces average token consumption by up to 35%.

title: TokenRouter: Uncertainty-Guided Token-Level Routing for Efficient LLM Reasoning

authors.text: Zhenning Shi, Yijia Zhu, Junhan Shi,
, Congcong Miao, Guorui Xie, Yong Jiang, Qing Li

summary: Letting small and large models share the work, one token at a time.
abstract: TokenRouter is a black-box runtime controller that allocates tokens between small and large language models. A robust entropy detector identifies difficult reasoning segments, while a self-calibrating policy controls the compute budget and a commitment mechanism prevents disruptive switching. Across three reasoning benchmarks, it preserves over 99% of pure-LLM accuracy with large-model activation on only 56.2% to 76.0% of generated tokens.
